subject: ScaleGrid: delayed scale propagation causing slot starvation — action plan
messages:
From: Priya Rao <pri@scalegrid.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, ops@scalegrid.com
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency & token timeouts during morning surge

Hi Jordan —

We started seeing a sustained latency spike in our dedicated GPU pool in us-west2 starting ~08:50 PDT. Token generation requests are intermittently timing out (client-level 30s), and many A/B test traffic lanes reported 4–8x tail latency. Our metrics show the autoscaler did not allocate additional reserved nodes for ~6 minutes despite queue depth increasing.

Attached is a short log excerpt (scalelog-20270809-0912.txt) that includes the time window and a failing request sample. Can you confirm whether this is related to the warmup pipeline or something on Redwood's autoscale/control plane?

Impact: highest for our inference-critical endpoints; some internal fallbacks triggered. We're pausing canary traffic until we understand the risk.

Appreciate a quick triage and expected ETA to stabilization.

— Priya
Platform & Reliability
ScaleGrid

Attachments: scalelog-20270809-0912.txt (text)
From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <pri@scalegrid.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High tail latency & token timeouts during morning surge

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the logs — I've looped in Soojin (SRE) and Ben (CS) to join the investigation and coordinate on mitigations. Initial read: queue depth spike + delayed scale decision looks like what we call "scale-propagation delay" where the control plane committed new allocations but the node join/registration lagged because of a concurrent rolling job in the us-west2 pool. We're triaging now.

Immediate steps we will take:
- Soojin will check node join/registration logs and trigger an expedited rejoin if required.
- If join time > 60s we will shift non-critical lanes to your us-west1 standby to reduce pressure while we perform a controlled restart.
- We'll prepare a short canary plan (pdf) and propose a brief maintenance window if needed.

I'll follow up within 45 minutes with a status update.

Sorry for the disruption — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: ScaleGrid us-west2 — triage notes and action items

Team — internal notes for the remediation path (do not forward to customer):

Observed: autoscaler issued allocations at 08:52:11; new nodes reported as "provisioned" but did not complete agent registration for ~5m 40s. During that gap, queue depth grew and the serving runtime experienced token timeouts on queued requests. Logs show multiple concurrent rolling operations (kernel patch push + image prewarm) overlapping node join.

Root cause hypothesis: orchestration race between rolling image warmups and node registration, exacerbated by our join timeout backoff which retries at expanding intervals. The control plane considered nodes provisioned (billing/commit) before runtime had fully attached caches and warmed kernels — so they were temporarily unable to accept low-latency requests.

Proposed mitigation (short window):
1) Immediate: expedite agent restart on the 3 slow join nodes (Soojin) to force re-registration; temporarily raise node-registration concurrency in us-west2 controller for 10 minutes.
2) Traffic shift: move non-critical lanes (A/B holdouts) to us-west1 standby — Ben to coordinate with customer on preservation of session affinity.
3) Canary: propose a small canary rollout with adjusted warmup (attach canary plan). If node joins still exceed 60s we'll enable conservative join-failure fallback (route to standby region automatically).
4) Postmortem: Naomi to own RCA writeup and credit recommendation; include quantification of impacted QPS and tail latency delta.

Please action 1 and 2 now and update this thread when complete. I'll craft the external update after we have confirmation.

-Jordan

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <pri@scalegrid.com>
Cc: ScaleGrid Platform Team <ops@scalegrid.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Update: root cause, remediation performed, and next steps (ScaleGrid us-west2)

Hi Priya —

Thank you again for the quick signal and logs. I wanted to summarize our findings, actions taken, and proposed follow-ups.

Summary / root cause:
- Between 08:50–08:59 PDT on Aug 9, certain nodes in your us-west2 dedicated pool were marked PROVISIONED by the control plane but failed to finish runtime agent registration due to a concurrent rolling image warmup job. The orchestration order meant control plane state advanced before runtime readiness checks completed, resulting in a ~5–7 minute window where new nodes existed but could not accept low-latency traffic. This led to increased queue depth and token timeouts for some requests.

Remediations performed (Aug 9):
- Force-restarted the runtime agent on the three slow join nodes and temporarily increased node-registration concurrency in the region to reduce retry backoff. (Completed 09:12–09:18 PDT.)
- Shifted non-critical A/B lanes to your us-west1 standby pool to reduce pressure while we stabilized the joins. (Completed 09:25 PDT.)
- Executed a controlled canary with adjusted warmup parameters overnight; full canary report attached (proposed-canary-plan.pdf).

Current status:
- The us-west2 pool has returned to normal join latencies and tail percentiles. We monitored for 48 hours post-fix and observed no recurrence during comparable traffic spikes.

Planned actions / prevention:
- Short term: we'll add an extra readiness gate in the provisioning flow so nodes are only marked AVAILABLE after runtime agent registration and KV cache warmup reach a minimal readiness threshold (target: within 90s).
- Medium term: change orchestration ordering to avoid overlapping rolling image warmups with heavy join waves and add faster-Path rejoin logic for late registrants.
- We'll add an automated traffic-routing fallback that moves non-critical lanes to standby region if node join latency exceeds 60s for more than two consecutive allocation events.

Credits & RCA deliverables:
- Naomi will produce a formal RCA doc and suggested service credit based on impacted QPS and duration; we expect to share this within 5 business days.
- Preliminary credit offer: one week of waived dedicated overage for the impacted lane (we will finalize after RCA quantification).

Attachments: proposed-canary-plan.pdf (outline of canary changes and monitoring thresholds)

If you prefer a short sync to walk through the changes or the canary report, Ben and I are available tomorrow morning. Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the flag and your patience while we tightened the node readiness checks.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
